title: Very ampleness descends along field extensions
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a scheme of finite type over $k$ and $\mathcal{L}$ an invertible module on $X$ such that $\mathcal{L}_K$ is very ample on $X_K$ for a field extension $K/k$. Then $\mathcal{L}$ is very ample on $X$; in particular $\mathcal{L}$ is ample if $\mathcal{L}_K$ is.

proof.text: By the definition of very ampleness, the hypothesis supplies the closed immersion $i_K:X_K\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(H^0(X_K,\mathcal L_K)^\vee)$ of the complete linear system, with $i_K^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L_K$. Hence $X_K$ is proper over $K$. Properness descends along the field extension by [lem-pc-proper-descends-field], so $X$ is proper over $k$.

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence and the assertion that the descended scheme is proper

proof.text: Since $X$ is now proper, flat coherent cohomology base change gives $H^0(X_K,\mathcal L_K)\cong H^0(X,\mathcal L)\otimes_kK$ by [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent]. Thus $H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ is finite-dimensional and, on taking $V:=H^0(X,\mathcal L)$, the defining space of $i_K$ is $V\otimes_kK$.

source.place: ## Proof, the equality of global sections after base change and finite coefficient extraction

proof.text: Let $V:=H^0(X,\mathcal L)$. The complete linear system of $\mathcal L$ defines a morphism $\psi:X\to\mathbf P(V^\vee)$, and its pullback of $\mathcal O(1)$ is $\mathcal L$. After base change along $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, the defining space becomes $V\otimes_kK=H^0(X_K,\mathcal L_K)$ by step 2, so the base-changed morphism is exactly $i_K$.

source.place: ## Proof, the finite section space and the projective morphism defined by it

proof.text: The sections in $V$ have no common zero on $X$: their common zero locus pulls back to the common zero locus of $V\otimes_kK=H^0(X_K,\mathcal L_K)$ on $X_K$, which is empty because $i_K$ is defined, and $X_K\to X$ is surjective. Therefore $\psi$ is defined. Use the fpqc covering of $\mathbf P(V^\vee)$ consisting of the single morphism $\mathbf P(V^\vee)_K\to\mathbf P(V^\vee)$, the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ (flat and surjective, with one affine quasi-compact member). Its pullback is $X\times_{\mathbf P(V^\vee)}\mathbf P(V^\vee)_K=X_K$, and the base change of $\psi$ is $i_K$ by [def-pc-base-change]. Hence [lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion] gives that $\psi$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: ## Proof, the descent of the closed immersion along the faithfully flat field extension

proof.text: The morphism $\psi$ is the morphism of the complete linear system of $\mathcal L$, and it is a closed immersion with $\psi^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L$. Thus $\mathcal L$ is very ample by [def-sc-ample]. Since [def-sc-ample] defines ample by requiring a positive tensor power to be very ample, very ampleness itself (the first power) implies that $\mathcal L$ is ample.
